Test Case: Registration page loads with step 1 of 5
Steps: 1) Open /register in a fresh incognito window 2) Observe the wizard
Expected Result: Step 1 'Hospital Identity' renders with a 5-step progress bar. No console errors.
Why This Exists: A hospital cannot become a customer if it cannot sign up. This is the very first screen anyone outside your company ever sees.

Steps: 1) Enter Hospital Name 'Aarogya Multispecialty Hospital' 2) Select Type 'Private Hospital' 3) Select State 'Telangana' 4) Select Bed Count '101-200 beds' 5) Enter Phone 9876500001 6) Click Next
Expected Result: Next is enabled and the wizard advances to step 2.
Why This Exists: Hospital type and bed count drive plan pricing and default module selection - wrong data here mis-prices the customer.

Test Case: Step 1 Next is disabled with any field blank
Steps: 1) Fill every field except State 2) Observe the Next button
Expected Result: Next stays disabled. No way to advance with incomplete identity.
Why This Exists: A hospital record without a state breaks GST place-of-supply and state scheme eligibility downstream.

Steps: 1) Enter phone 98765 2) Try Next 3) Enter 98765000011 (11 digits) 4) Try Next 5) Enter 9876500001 6) Try Next
Expected Result: Only the 10-digit value is accepted. Shorter and longer are rejected.
Why This Exists: Indian mobile numbers are 10 digits. A malformed number means OTP and WhatsApp never reach the customer.

Steps: 1) Type 'abcdefghij' into Phone 2) Type '98765-0001'
Expected Result: Non-numeric input is rejected or stripped.
Why This Exists: Free-text phone fields are the most common source of unusable contact data.

Test Case: Phone OTP is sent and verifies
Steps: 1) Complete step 1 with phone 9876500001 2) Click Verify 3) Retrieve the OTP 4) Enter it 5) Submit
Expected Result: OTP accepted, phone shows verified, and a single-use token is held for the final submit.
Notes: If OTP is not enabled on your platform settings this case is N/A - mark BLOCKED and note it
Why This Exists: OTP is the only thing stopping bulk fake signups from consuming your free trials.

Steps: 1) Request an OTP 2) Enter 000000 3) Submit
Expected Result: Rejected with a clear message. Phone stays unverified. Registration cannot proceed.
Why This Exists: An OTP that accepts any value is the same as having no OTP at all.

Steps: 1) Request an OTP 2) Wait past the expiry window 3) Enter the correct code 4) Submit
Expected Result: Rejected as expired. A new OTP must be requested.
Why This Exists: An OTP with no expiry can be reused indefinitely if intercepted.

Steps: 1) Password TestPass@2026 2) Confirm TestPass@2025 3) Next

Test Case: Step 1 Branding saves logo and colour

Expected Result: Billing loads. Day closure is NOT in the billing_staff route list - it must be blocked.
Notes: ROUTE_ROLES['/billing/closure'] excludes billing_staff
Why This Exists: Day closure locks the cash books. Only a senior person should be able to close a day.

Steps: 1) As +qa.accountant.a visit /accounts /accounts/chart-of-accounts /accounts/journal-workbench
Expected Result: All load.
Why This Exists: The accountant needs the ledger.

Test Case: accountant is blocked from clinical routes
Steps: 1) As +qa.accountant.a try /opd /ipd /patients /lab
Expected Result: All blocked.
Why This Exists: Finance staff have no clinical need and no consent basis to view patient records.

Steps: 1) As +qa.cfo.a visit /accounts/financial-statements /accounts/budget /accounts/fixed-assets /analytics/revenue-intelligence
Expected Result: All load.
Why This Exists: The CFO's whole job is these four screens.

Test Case: cfo is blocked from clinical routes
Steps: 1) As +qa.cfo.a try /opd /ipd /patients
Expected Result: Blocked.
Why This Exists: Seniority is not a clinical need. DPDP purpose limitation applies to the CFO too.

Steps: 1) As +qa.hr.a visit /hr 2) Then try /opd /billing /accounts
Expected Result: HR loads. The others are blocked.
Why This Exists: HR needs staff data, not patient or financial data.

Steps: 1) As +qa.insurance.a visit /insurance 2) Then try /hr /accounts
Expected Result: Insurance loads. The others are blocked.
Why This Exists: Insurance desk staff work claims, nothing else.

Steps: 1) As +qa.mrd.a visit /mrd 2) Then try /billing /hr
Expected Result: MRD loads. The others are blocked.
Why This Exists: MRD sees every record by definition - so everything else must be closed to them.

Steps: 1) As each of the 16 roles visit /dashboard /modules /settings/profile /inbox /my-hr
Expected Result: All load for every role.
Notes: coreRoutes are open to every authenticated user
Why This Exists: Every employee needs their own profile and payslips regardless of role.

Steps: 1) As +qa.admin.a (hospital_admin) navigate to /platform
Expected Result: Blocked. Platform is your SaaS console not the hospital's.
Why This Exists: A hospital admin reaching the platform console could change their own plan or see other hospitals.

Steps: 1) Try /platform as all 16 non-super-admin roles
Expected Result: All blocked.
Why This Exists: One role slipping through exposes every hospital on the system, not just this one.

Steps: 1) Log in as +qa.superadmin 2) Visit /platform and its sub-routes
Expected Result: All load.
Why This Exists: You need the console to run the business.

Test Case: Blocked route does not flash data before redirecting
Steps: 1) As +qa.nurse.a navigate to /accounts 2) Watch closely and check the network tab
Expected Result: No financial data renders even briefly and no data request is made.
Notes: A client-only redirect that still fetches is a real leak
Why This Exists: A screen that renders then redirects has already sent the data to the browser - it is a leak even if the user only sees it for a moment.

Test Case: Role change takes effect on next login
Steps: 1) Change +qa.nurse.a from nurse to billing_executive 2) Have them log out and back in 3) Try /billing
Expected Result: Billing now accessible; nursing routes now blocked.
Notes: Change it back afterwards
Why This Exists: Permissions that do not update leave a transferred employee with their old access indefinitely.

Test Case: Custom permission blob overrides the static role
Steps: 1) Settings > Roles 2) Grant nurse view access to billing 3) As the nurse open /billing
Expected Result: Access granted. When a permissions row exists it is used INSTEAD of the static role list, not in addition.
Notes: hasAccess uses ONLY permissions when a row exists - no static fallthrough
Why This Exists: Hospitals genuinely need custom roles. But because the blob replaces rather than extends the defaults, a partially-filled blob silently removes access the role used to have.

Steps: 1) Set a role's permissions to an empty object 2) Log in as that role 3) Try any module route
Expected Result: All module routes denied. Only core routes remain.
Notes: Deliberate - a role with zero permissions is denied not defaulted
Why This Exists: If an empty permission set fell back to defaults, revoking someone's access would silently do nothing.

Steps: 1) Remove billing view from the modified nurse role 2) Log in again 3) Try /billing
Expected Result: Blocked again.
Why This Exists: Granting access is easy. Revoking it is what matters when someone changes job or leaves.

Test Case: Per-user override withholds from one person
Steps: 1) Apply a user_permission_overrides withhold to one doctor 2) Log in as them 3) Compare with the other doctor
Expected Result: Only the overridden user loses that access.
Why This Exists: Sometimes one individual needs restricting without changing the whole role - e.g. a doctor under investigation.

Test Case: URL with a query string resolves the same
Steps: 1) As +qa.nurse.a try /accounts?tab=journals
Expected Result: Blocked identically to /accounts.
Notes: Path is normalised by splitting on ?
Why This Exists: Appending a query string is the most obvious way to try to slip past a naive path check.

Steps: 1) As +qa.nurse.a try /accounts/
Expected Result: Blocked identically.
Why This Exists: Same reasoning - path normalisation must be complete or it is not a control.

Test Case: Unknown route shows 404 not a crash
Steps: 1) Visit /this-route-does-not-exist
Expected Result: Clean NotFound page. No stack trace or blank screen.
Why This Exists: A stack trace on screen tells an attacker what framework and structure you use.

Test Case: Sidebar hides routes the role cannot open
Steps: 1) As each role inspect the sidebar
Expected Result: Only permitted modules appear. No visible link leads to a blocked page.
Why This Exists: Showing a link that then denies access makes the product feel broken and generates support calls.

Steps: 1) As +qa.nurse.a open /modules 2) Click every tile shown
Expected Result: Every tile shown actually opens.
Why This Exists: The modules grid is how a new user explores the product. Dead tiles destroy confidence immediately.

Steps: 1) Check whether quality_officer or quality_manager can be assigned 2) If not, verify who can open /quality /nabh/compliance /ipc/dashboard
Expected Result: Document who can actually reach these. ROUTE_ROLES names roles that are not in the app_role enum.
Notes: Directly related to TC-P1D-015
Why This Exists: The Quality module names quality_officer as its user but that role cannot exist. Either the enum is missing values or the routing is wrong - both are real defects.

Test Case: Blood Bank / CSSD / Dialysis role reachability
Steps: 1) Confirm blood_bank_technician, cssd_technician and dialysis_technician cannot be assigned 2) Determine who can actually open /blood-bank /cssd /dialysis
Expected Result: Document the effective access.
Why This Exists: These modules list a specialist as the intended user but only admins can reach them - meaning the actual technician cannot do their job.

Steps: 1) For 5 roles compare what the sidebar shows against what direct URL entry allows
Expected Result: The two agree exactly in both directions.
Why This Exists: A route hidden in the nav but reachable by URL is security by obscurity, which is no security.

Test Case: Browser Back after a block does not grant access
Steps: 1) As nurse open /nursing 2) Try /accounts (blocked) 3) Press Back twice
Expected Result: Never lands on an accessible /accounts.
Why This Exists: History navigation is a classic way client-side guards get bypassed.

Steps: 1) As +qa.reception.a open an OPD consultation 2) Look for the Complete & Bill action
Expected Result: The action is not rendered.
Notes: hasActionAccess('opd','complete_bill')
Why This Exists: Only a doctor should be able to declare a consultation complete - it closes the clinical record and triggers billing.

Steps: 1) As +qa.reception.a open a consultation 2) Look for the Admit action
Expected Result: Not rendered.
Notes: hasActionAccess('opd','admit_patient')
Why This Exists: Admission is a clinical decision with major financial consequences for the patient.

Test Case: Doctor CAN see Complete & Bill and Admit
Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a open a consultation
Expected Result: Both actions are rendered.
Why This Exists: The counterpart to the two cases above - the gate must permit as reliably as it denies.

Steps: 1) As +qa.nurse.a open the discount approvals inbox if reachable
Expected Result: Either not reachable or the Approve action is absent.
Why This Exists: Discount approval is a financial authority. Anyone able to approve can give money away.

Test Case: Tabs within a module are individually gated
Steps: 1) As +qa.reception.a open OPD 2) List the visible tabs 3) Repeat as +qa.doctor.a
Expected Result: The two see different tab sets appropriate to their role.
Notes: hasTabAccess from src/lib/tabPermissions.ts
Why This Exists: A receptionist seeing the clinical examination tab can read and alter medical findings.

Test Case: Platform entitlement floor overrides even super_admin
Steps: 1) Identify an action gated by the platform entitlement floor 2) Attempt it as super_admin
Expected Result: Still withheld. The floor cannot be overridden locally.
Notes: tabPermissions.ts lines ~557-666
Why This Exists: This is how you enforce plan limits. If a super admin could bypass it, entitlements would be unenforceable.

Test Case: Hidden action cannot be triggered by other means
Steps: 1) As +qa.reception.a with Complete & Bill hidden, attempt the same operation via keyboard shortcut or a crafted request
Expected Result: Rejected server-side as well as hidden in the UI.
Notes: Hiding a button is not access control unless the server also refuses
Why This Exists: A button hidden only in the UI is not a permission - anyone who opens DevTools can still call the underlying operation.

Steps: 1) As several roles look for export or download actions on patient and financial lists
Expected Result: Only permitted roles see them.
Why This Exists: Bulk export is how data leaves an organisation. It needs tighter control than viewing.

Steps: 1) As non-admin roles look for delete actions on master data
Expected Result: Not available to non-admin roles.
Why This Exists: Deleted master data breaks every historical record that referenced it.

Steps: 1) Grant a role view-only on a module 2) Confirm it can read but not create or edit
Expected Result: Read works; write actions are absent.
Why This Exists: Many roles legitimately need to see without changing - an auditor, a trainee, a referring doctor.

Test Case: Legacy string permission format still resolves
Steps: 1) If any role has a legacy 'r' or 'rw' string permission verify it resolves
Expected Result: 'r' grants view; 'rw' grants view/create/edit/delete.
Notes: Backward compatibility path in hasPermission
Why This Exists: Older hospitals will have legacy permission blobs. If they stop resolving, existing customers lose access overnight.

Steps: 1) Check a specialty module such as /dialysis with a blob that only names its legacy parent
Expected Result: Resolves via LEGACY_MODULE_PARENT.
Why This Exists: Specialty modules used to inherit a parent bucket. Breaking the fallback silently removes access for every existing customer.

Steps: 1) As Hospital A (Professional) open the modules included in that plan
Expected Result: All load.
Why This Exists: The customer must get what they paid for.

Steps: 1) As Hospital B (Starter) try to open a Professional-only module
Expected Result: Blocked by ModuleGate with an upgrade message rather than a raw error.
Why This Exists: If the plan is not enforced, nobody has any reason to upgrade.

Test Case: Plan gate applies to direct URL entry
Steps: 1) As Hospital B paste a blocked module URL directly
Expected Result: Blocked identically to clicking.
Notes: ModuleGate wraps the AppShell Outlet so every route is enforced
Why This Exists: A gate that only works from the menu is not a gate.

Test Case: Upgrading a plan unlocks modules immediately
Steps: 1) As super admin upgrade Hospital B to Professional 2) Refresh Hospital B's session 3) Open a previously blocked module
Expected Result: Now accessible.
Notes: Realtime channel listens on hospital_module_entitlements
Why This Exists: A customer who pays for an upgrade and cannot use it for a day will ask for a refund.

Steps: 1) Downgrade Hospital B back to Starter 2) Refresh 3) Try the module again
Expected Result: Blocked again. Existing data is preserved not deleted.
Notes: Data must survive a downgrade
Why This Exists: A downgrade that deletes data makes downgrading catastrophic and traps customers - or loses them permanently.

Test Case: Addon withhold hides a single AI feature
Steps: 1) Withhold one AI feature key from Hospital A 2) Open the screen that uses it
Expected Result: That AI action is not rendered. Others still are.
Notes: AI features are actions of the pseudo-module ai_suite
Why This Exists: AI features are priced individually. Withholding must be surgical, not all-or-nothing.

Test Case: AI master toggle hides all AI features
Steps: 1) Turn off the AI Features master toggle 2) Check several AI-bearing screens
Expected Result: All AI actions hidden.
Why This Exists: Some hospitals will not permit AI on clinical records at all. One switch must satisfy that.

Test Case: Expired subscription applies a write lock
Steps: 1) Set Hospital B's subscription to expired 2) Try to create any record
Expected Result: Reads still work; writes are blocked with a clear renewal message.
Notes: src/lib/subscriptionLock.ts
Why This Exists: Non-payment must stop new work without destroying access to existing records - a hospital still needs to read its own patient history.

Steps: 1) With Hospital B expired open a patient record
Expected Result: Record is readable.
Why This Exists: Blocking read access to medical records over a billing dispute would be a patient-safety issue and probably unlawful.

Steps: 1) Set Hospital B's trial to expired 2) Attempt a write
Expected Result: Same write lock as a paid expiry.
Why This Exists: An unlimited trial is a free product.

Test Case: Blocked module shows an upgrade path not an error
Steps: 1) Trigger any plan block 2) Read the message
Expected Result: Clear explanation and a route to upgrade. Not a stack trace or blank page.
Why This Exists: A gate is also a sales opportunity. A raw error is just a bad experience.

Steps: 1) If entitlement resolution fails check entitlement_fail_open_events
Expected Result: Any fail-open is recorded for review.
Notes: Fail-open is safer than locking a hospital out but must be visible
Why This Exists: Failing open keeps hospitals working during an outage, but an unlogged fail-open means customers silently get free features forever.

Test Case: Hospital A cannot list Hospital B patients
Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a open /patients 2) Search for PT-QA-0030 and 'Rohan Kulkarni'
Expected Result: No result. Hospital B's patient is invisible.
Why This Exists: One hospital seeing another's patients is a reportable data breach that ends the company.

Test Case: Hospital A cannot open a Hospital B patient by UUID
Steps: 1) Get PT-QA-0030's UUID from the DB 2) As +qa.doctor.a paste /patients/<uuid>/summary
Expected Result: Blocked or not found. NOTE: no PHI must render even briefly.
Notes: The classic IDOR test
Why This Exists: Guessing or leaking a record ID is the most common way multi-tenant systems leak data.

Test Case: Direct API query returns no cross-tenant rows
Steps: 1) In the browser console as +qa.doctor.a run a supabase select on patients with no filter 2) Inspect the rows
Expected Result: Only Hospital A rows return. RLS enforces this at the database.
Notes: This is the real test - the UI filter is not the control, RLS is
Why This Exists: Anyone can open DevTools and query directly. If RLS is not the boundary, the UI filter is decoration.

Steps: 1) As +qa.billing.a query bills directly with no filter
Expected Result: Only Hospital A bills.
Why This Exists: Another hospital's revenue figures are commercially sensitive as well as confidential.

Steps: 1) As +qa.insurance.a query insurance_claims directly
Expected Result: Only Hospital A rows. NOTE: this query has NO hospital_id filter in the code and relies entirely on RLS.
Notes: ClaimsStatus.tsx line 128 - highest-risk query in the app
Why This Exists: This is one of two places found that fetch without a hospital filter. If RLS is ever misconfigured, this leaks first.

Steps: 1) As +qa.insurance.a query denial_logs directly
Expected Result: Only Hospital A rows.
Notes: ClaimsStatus.tsx line 170 - same risk as above
Why This Exists: Second of the two unfiltered queries. Same exposure.

Test Case: Cross-tenant isolation on admissions and beds
Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a query admissions and beds directly
Expected Result: Only Hospital A rows.
Why This Exists: Bed occupancy is operationally sensitive and the admissions table carries diagnoses.

Test Case: Cross-tenant isolation on prescriptions and lab_orders
Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a query prescriptions and lab_orders directly
Expected Result: Only Hospital A rows.
Why This Exists: Prescriptions and results are the most sensitive category of health data.

Test Case: Cross-tenant isolation on users and staff
Steps: 1) As +qa.admin.a query users directly
Expected Result: Only Hospital A staff.
Why This Exists: Staff names and emails of another hospital are both a privacy issue and a competitive one.

Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a attempt to insert a row with Hospital B's hospital_id
Expected Result: Rejected by RLS.
Why This Exists: Reading another tenant's data is bad. Writing into it is worse - it corrupts their records.

Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a attempt to update a Hospital B patient row by UUID
Expected Result: Rejected. Row unchanged.
Why This Exists: An attacker who cannot read but can write can still destroy another hospital's records.

Test Case: Stale session context after a hospital move
Steps: 1) Note the hms_ctx_* sessionStorage key as +qa.doctor.a 2) As super admin move that user to Hospital B 3) WITHOUT logging out refresh the page 4) Observe which hospital's data shows
Expected Result: Must resolve to Hospital B or force a re-auth. NOTE: the cache is only cleared on sign-out, so this may show stale Hospital A data - if so, log P1.
Notes: HospitalContext caches in sessionStorage and revalidates in the background
Why This Exists: A user moved between hospitals who keeps the old tenant is actively looking at the wrong hospital's patients.

Test Case: Service role key is not in the client bundle
Steps: 1) Build the app 2) Search dist/ for the service role key and for 'service_role'
Expected Result: Not present anywhere in the client bundle.
Notes: npm run build then grep dist/
Why This Exists: The service role key bypasses all RLS. If it ships to the browser, every tenant boundary in the product is gone.

Steps: 1) Log in and walk OPD IPD and Billing with the console open 2) Review every logged line
Expected Result: No patient name UHID phone or diagnosis appears in any console message.
Notes: DPDP requirement - PHI must not appear in logs
Why This Exists: Console logs get captured by browser extensions, error trackers and screen shares. PHI there is a breach.

Test Case: Error messages do not leak PHI
Steps: 1) Deliberately trigger errors (bad ID, blocked action) 2) Read every message
Expected Result: Messages are generic. No patient identifiers or SQL fragments.
Why This Exists: Error messages are shown to users and logged to third-party services. Both are places PHI must never reach.

Steps: 1) Create a bill in Hospital A and one in Hospital B 2) Compare the numbers
Expected Result: Independent sequences. Neither continues the other's numbering.
Notes: bill_sequences is keyed per hospital
Why This Exists: Shared invoice numbering between two hospitals means duplicate invoice numbers under different GSTINs - a tax compliance failure.

Steps: 1) As +qa.admin.a open /admin/go-live
Expected Result: Loads with the checklist.
Why This Exists: This is the hospital's own readiness gate before they start using the system for real patients.

Steps: 1) With departments and wards configured but no drugs 2) Review the checklist
Expected Result: Completed items show complete; the drug item shows incomplete.
Why This Exists: A checklist that does not check anything is theatre. It must read the real state.

Test Case: Checklist items link to the right settings screen
Steps: 1) Click an incomplete item
Expected Result: Navigates to the screen that fixes it.
Why This Exists: Telling someone what is missing without showing them where to fix it just creates a support call.

Steps: 1) As +qa.doctor.a navigate to /admin/go-live
Expected Result: Blocked.
Why This Exists: Declaring a hospital live is an administrative decision.

Steps: 1) Remove rate_per_day from a ward 2) Remove all consultation fees 3) Review the checklist
Expected Result: These should be flagged. NOTE: if the checklist passes without them, log P1 - these are the two silent Rs 500 fallbacks.
Notes: The two most damaging silent failures in the product
Why This Exists: A hospital going live without consultation fees or room rates will under-bill every single patient and not know for months.

Steps: 1) As +qa.admin.a open /admin/data-migration
Expected Result: Loads.
Why This Exists: Every hospital switching from another system needs to bring its patient list with it. This is often the deal-breaker.
